US Emerging Internet
US Internet: AI bear narratives compound, but finding a floor?

Mark Shmulik
+1 917 344 8508

Internet stocks have de-rated on a combination of rotation away from tech and worsening AI sentiment (both too much CapEx and too much disruption risk). Bearish narratives have packed a bigger punch than efforts to defend the incumbents. Internally, we have debated the degree to which the de-rating can continue, internalizing the Internet testament that “it can always go lower”. And while we haven’t sensed investor urgency to step in yet and own the basket, GAAP P/E multiples are reasonable, and we may well be entering the trough of AI disruption disillusionment on the consumer side given adoption timelines and enterprise focus from the leading labs. All the while, incumbent earnings could continue to be solid.
Hitting trough Adj. EBITDA levels, with GAAP P/E multiples also increasingly reasonable. The median EV/NTM Adj. EBITDA multiple for our Internet basket has compressed from 16x in November to \~12x currently. This is in-line with recent trough levels (Exhibit 4). We appreciate that “Adjusted EBITDA” offers little comfort in a market that is scrutinizing SBC and earnings quality. The median 2027E GAAP P/E multiple now also sits at 22.5x vs. the S&P500 at 20x (Exhibit 6). There’s more of a GAAP earnings floor to the group than we’ve seen in prior years (a notable shift for the SMID-Cap names). The implied PEG ratio for the group is 0.8x vs. the broader market at 1.4x (we use a 2YR CAGR in forecasts to avoid one-timers and dilute the effect of growth off a small base). Admittedly, the Mega-Caps aren’t cheap on FCF multiples given CapEx dynamics.
Compounding narratives. Reasons for the recent de-rating include: (1) KPI revisions stagnating or turning negative (e.g., modestly negative EBITDA revisions in Rideshare/ Delivery and mega-cap tech investing substantial FCF into data center capacity); (2) rotation to other sectors offering cyclical torque and revision upside; (3) the AI pain trade, covering both Software and Consumer Internet on the long-term disintermediation risk from AI + broader macro risks from white collar work disruption. The market is clearly debating the multi-year durability of these business models, not the next few quarters.
What gets the AI pain trade to reverse? Changing consumer behavior is really hard. And monetizing those changes? Really, really hard. Given the torque Anthropic has seen ramping their enterprise revenue run-rate, alongside recent OpenAI product and partnership announcements, it is plausible OpenAI may look to prioritize B2B > Consumer in the near-term. Outside a shock competitive dynamics shift, the AI pain trade probably take longer to shake off, as we’ve seen when fighting terminal value debates (e.g., UBER and AVs). We won’t pretend to have the silver bullet. The world is moving quickly, and the nature of software and technology development is changing.
Any extension of timelines around AGI capabilities is probably good for the Consumer Internet basket (ex-Cloud). Shifting timelines can offer some reprieve, but to structurally re-rate we think the sector needs to start generating “AI revenue” which could take various forms (e.g., the GOOGL turnaround). For the big capital spenders, indication of durable ROIC from the spending beyond bare metal rentals should alleviation doomsday value destruction fears. For many marketplaces, vertically integrated AI assistants (akin to AMZN and Rufus) may be the necessary next step to shift the narrative and regain the “AI winner” tag. Longer-term, business models may have to evolve, but they’ve always evolved.

INVESTMENT IMPLICATIONS On US Emerging Internet, we rate DASH, ZG, UBER, and CART Outperform. On US Internet, we rate META, AMZN, and PINS Outperform. We rate the rest of our coverage Market-Perform. Valuation alone is not a catalyst in this sector, but offers some perspective on where things currently stand following the sell-off. Considering much of the space has been put in the ‘at risk’ camp from AI, any stumbles along the way on timing or fundamental impact with respect to the bear case could improve sentiment for the broader Consumer Internet basket. Conversely, the Mega-Caps need to deliver some combination of AI ROI, FCF re-acceleration, and enough support to confirm the moats around their core businesses are still intact, ideally strengthened by the application of AI. 2 on 05-Mar-2026 Nikhil Devnani, CFA    +1 917 344 8425  nikhil.devnani@bernsteinsg.com 5 March 2026 US EMERGING INTERNET BERNSTEIN|SOCIETE CENERALECROUP
